assessments.reasoning: The FSF's 1.3 §1 at [3605,5049) defines Transparent and Opaque. Section 3 at [8127,8910) fixes the unit of delivery, download audience, content, protocol and time conditions. It has no Cover Text notice or printed-medium prerequisite.

limitations: Section 1 assesses the representation's public specification, suitability for ordinary revision and processing, and barriers to modification. Even a PDF can vary in status according to how it was made. A file extension alone cannot settle classification.

The prudence of particular measures and whether particular access controls allow general public access require facts. The absence of express anonymity and price terms in 1.3 does not resolve every registration or fee arrangement.
reasoning: Publishing or distributing more than 100 Opaque copies under 1.3 §3 requires a machine-readable Transparent copy with each Opaque copy or a location identified in or with each copy. At that location the general network-using public must be able to download the complete Transparent Document without added material through public-standard protocols. On choosing that route, the distributor must take reasonably prudent steps as quantity distribution begins to maintain access there through at least one year after its last public distribution of an Opaque copy of that edition, including distribution through its agents or retailers.
